arguments.text:
Fixed the `src/interval.js` bug in `Interval.fromISO`.

Root cause: the method called `DateTime.fromISO(s, opts)` / `DateTime.fromISO(e, opts)` directly. When `Settings.throwOnInvalid` is true, parsing the duration half of an interval (e.g. `"2016-01-01/P1Y"` or `"P1Y/2016-01-01"`) throws an InvalidDateTimeError before the code can fall back to `Duration.fromISO`, so valid duration/date intervals blew up instead of being built.

Fix: wrap both `DateTime.fromISO` calls in try/catch and track validity in `startIsValid` / `endIsValid` flags, so the duration fallbacks (`Interval.after` / `Interval.before`) still run under `throwOnInvalid`. (Also fixed the message typo "asISO 8601" -> "as ISO 8601" in the unparsable explanation.)

Verified: `Interval.fromISO("2016-01-01/2016-12-31")`, `"2016-01-01/P1Y"`, `"P1Y/2016-01-01"` all return valid intervals with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true` (checked with a temporary test, now removed). Full suite: 893 passed, only the 2 pre-existing failures in `test/datetime/toFormat.test.js` (French locale formatting, unrelated and failing before my change) remain.

arguments.text:
#2 is fixed and verified.

Root cause: `objToLocalTS` in `src/impl/util.js` handled the "years 0-99 are read as 19XX" legacy quirk by computing the timestamp with `Date.UTC(...)` and then subtracting 1900 from the resulting year (`d.setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1900)`). When the day-of-month overflowed past February, the intermediate date was computed in 1999/2000 — a leap year — so the extra Feb 29 was carried over into year 100 (not a leap year), shifting the result by one day.

Fix: re-apply the month and day when correcting the year, i.e. `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`.

Verified: `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ months: 2 })` => 0100-02-28, `plus({ days: 61 })` => 0100-03-02, `plus({ days: 60 })` => 0100-02-28, `plus({ months: 14 })` => 0101-02-28. I also ran a differential sweep (days/weeks/months/years additions from every month-end in years 0-99 against a proleptic-Gregorian reference): 0 mismatches. Full suite: 892 passed, only the same 2 pre-existing `toFormat` locale failures.

#4 is fixed and verified.

Root cause: `DateTime#isInDST` in `src/datetime.js` compared `this.offset` with `this.set({ month: 1 }).offset`, i.e. the *same day-of-month* in January. In years where DST is already in effect in early January (e.g. the 1974 US year-round DST, Jan 6 - Oct 27), that comparison is against a DST date itself, so it returned false.

Fix: compare against January 1st instead — `this.set({ month: 1, day: 1 }).offset` — which is standard time in the northern hemisphere.

Verified with `America/New_York` 1974: Jan 6/Jan 7 through Oct 27 report `isInDST === true`, Jan 5 and Oct 28 report false; a sweep of all 365 days of 1974 matches the offset-based truth exactly. Southern-hemisphere zones (Australia/Sydney) and Europe/Paris still report correctly, and the existing `isInDST` tests still pass. Full suite: 892 passed, only the same 2 pre-existing `toFormat` locale failures.

#5 is fixed and verified.

Root cause: the conversion matrices in `src/duration.js` were missing entries, so `convert()` computed `undefined` conversions and produced `NaN`:
- `casualMatrix.years` had no `quarters` entry (and `accurateMatrix.years` neither)
- `casualMatrix.quarters` had no `seconds` entry

So `Duration.fromObject({ years: 1, quarters: 1 }).normalize()` and `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 1 }).normalize()` returned NaN values.

Fix: added `quarters: 4` to the `years` block of both the casual and accurate matrices, and `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60` to the casual `quarters` block (the accurate one already had it).

Verified: a probe over all 81 unit pairs now yields 0 NaN results for both `normalize()` and `shiftTo()`; `years -> quarters` = 4, `quarters -> seconds` = 7862400, `{years:1, quarters:1}.normalize()` = `{years:1, quarters:1}`. Full suite: 892 passed, only the same 2 pre-existing `toFormat` locale failures.
#2 fixed and verified (objToLocalTS year-100 / February overflow).
#4 fixed and verified (DateTime#isInDST for 1974 US year-round DST).
#5 fixed and verified (Duration conversion matrix missing years->quarters and quarters->seconds).

#7 is fixed and verified.

Root cause: `padStart` in `src/impl/util.js` padded by string length, so the minus sign of a negative number was counted as a digit: `padStart(-5, 4)` returned `"00-5"` (and `padStart(-100, 4)` returned `"-100"`). That leaked into `DateTime#toISODate()` (and `toISO`/`toISOWeekDate`/`toFormat("yyyy")`), which produced `"00-5-05-25"` for year -5 instead of `"-0005-05-25"`.

Fix: pad the absolute value and re-attach the sign, i.e. `"-" + ("" + -input).padStart(n, "0")` for negative input, so the sign is not part of the padded width.

Verified: `padStart(-5,4)` => `-0005`, `padStart(-100,4)` => `-0100`, `padStart(-118040,4)` => `-118040` (unchanged, no truncation); `toISODate()` for years -5/-100/-118040 => `-0005-05-25` / `-0100-05-25` / `-118040-05-25`, and the existing `[±YYYYY]` test still passes. Full suite: 892 passed, only the same 2 pre-existing `toFormat` locale failures.

#8 is fixed and verified.

Root cause: `FixedOffsetZone#isValid` in `src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js` was hard-coded to `return true`, so a zone built from a non-numeric offset (e.g. `new FixedOffsetZone("blorp")` or `FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp")`) claimed to be valid. Because the `DateTime` constructor only marks itself invalid when `!zone.isValid`, such a DateTime stayed "valid" while carrying a NaN offset.

Fix: `get isValid() { return isNumber(this.fixed); }` (importing `isNumber` from `src/impl/util.js`).

Verified: `new FixedOffsetZone("blorp")`, `(undefined)`, `(null)` and `("60")` are all invalid, while numeric offsets and `utcInstance` remain valid; `DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone: new FixedOffsetZone("blorp") })` and `DateTime.fromObject({ year: 2020, zone: FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp") })` are now invalid with reason "unsupported zone", and valid fixed zones (`UTC`, `UTC+5`, `FixedOffsetZone.instance(300)`) still work. Full suite: 892 passed, only the same 2 pre-existing `toFormat` locale failures.
